<reason>Side A won a close, high-quality clash by holding a stable distinction between inherited form and vendor package, so expense did not cancel a public kin-facing duty. Side B was sharper on lived enforcement and uncapped sting, but overreached by letting a no-kin elopement pay the remaining debt and collapsing recognition into production, which made “little obligation” less modest than advertised and left A's keep-the-form comparison as the cleaner vote.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's R2 answers to B's pressure: a costly family-facing ceremony still serves household merger, and “be seen as married” is not “rent two hundred chairs,” blocking B's onlooker-tax trap and exposing the elopement fork.</best_rebuttal>
